Research

Two papers on how people and AI systems work together.

Behavioural & Social SciencesIRIS National Fair submission

Do students trust AI too much?

I had 168 students in Grades 7–9 solve problems with help from an AI, then checked when they believed it and whether it was actually right.

Overall

45%38%17%
Got it rightTrusted a wrong answerDoubted a right answer

Easy vs hard problems

Easy
78%
Hard
19%64%17%
In short: the harder the problem, the more students just believed the AI, even when it was wrong.

Projects

Two live tools I built to teach and measure reasoning. Both are open to try.

NLP · Live demo

Reasoning Evaluator (ScienceBridge AI)

Paste a student’s argument and the Argument Intelligence Analyzer scores the quality of its reasoning, looking at logical structure, depth, evidence and clarity.

  • Model: transformer-based NLP, trained on 45K+ argument-quality samples
  • Result: 0.15 RMSE on evaluation
  • Hosted on: Hugging Face Spaces

Education · Live platform

Logical: 3D Knowledge Continuum

A gamified critical-thinking platform where students move through 15 interactive 3D stages, from observation and basic logic to pattern intelligence and analytical thinking, earning XP and unlocking artifacts as they go.

  • Built for: school students in ScienceTech Foothold sessions
  • Structure: 15 staged nodes with XP, credits and a progress tracker

Writing

Essay · John Locke Global Essay Competition

Should we be polite to ChatGPT?

The AI has no feelings to hurt, so the case for being polite rests on what it does for the person typing. Written for the John Locke Global Essay Competition.

  • 1
    Clearer requestsCourteous, well-framed prompts cut ambiguity, so the model understands the intent and answers better.
  • 2
    Better habitsTone transfers. Respectful language with AI supports how we speak to people.
  • 3
    Safer useFraming shapes the answer, and decorum supports responsible use, especially on sensitive topics or with younger users.

The catch: politeness shouldn’t slide into treating the AI as a person, which skews what we expect from it.
